questions.question: If a metal spoon and a wooden bowl are left in a classroom overnight, what will be true about their temperatures in the morning?
options: The metal spoon will be much colder than the wooden bowl
The wooden bowl will be warmer than the room
Both objects will have reached the exact same temperature as the room
The metal spoon will have a higher temperature than the room

questions.question: When you heat a solid block of copper, what happens to the motion of its particles?
options: They begin to move freely from place to place
They vibrate more quickly about their fixed positions
They stop moving entirely
They slow down their vibrations

questions.question: What is the primary physical consequence of heating a solid or a liquid?
options: Its mass increases
It contracts in volume
It causes the substance to expand
Its particles become tightly bound together

questions.question: Under which condition will a freshly brewed mug of hot tea cool down at the fastest rate?
options: When placed in a room that is very cold
When placed in a room that is almost as hot as the tea
When wrapped in a thick woollen sleeve
When the temperature of the tea is close to the room temperature

questions.question: Why do different substances behave differently when heated, in terms of particle interactions?
options: All substances have identical particle masses but different temperatures
The mass of particles and the attractive forces between them vary across different substances
Particles in some substances do not experience any attractive forces
Only liquids have attractive forces between their particles

questions.question: If Substance A has a higher specific heat capacity than Substance B, what does this mean for 1 kg of each substance at 50ºC?
options: Substance A has less energy in its thermal store than Substance B
Substance A has more energy in its thermal store than Substance B
Both substances store the exact same amount of thermal energy
Substance A will instantly cool down to 0ºC

questions.question: In which states of matter do the particles move or vibrate in random directions?
options: Only in gases
Only in liquids and gases
Solids, liquids, and gases
Only in solids

questions.question: Two copper blocks are both at a temperature of 80ºC. Block X has a mass of 2 kg, while Block Y has a mass of 1 kg. Which block has more energy in its thermal store?
options: Block Y, because smaller objects retain heat better
They both have the same energy because their temperatures are equal
Block X, because it contains more particles
Neither block has any thermal energy because they are solids

questions.question: To ensure an accurate reading when using a glass thermometer, how should you position your eyes?
options: Look down at the thermometer from directly above
Look up at the thermometer from a low angle
Position your eye level with the top of the coloured liquid
Hold the thermometer at arm's length and look at it sideways

questions.question: What are the melting point of pure ice and the boiling point of pure water under standard conditions?
options: Melting point is 0ºC, boiling point is 50ºC
Melting point is 10ºC, boiling point is 100ºC
Melting point is 0ºC, boiling point is 100ºC
Melting point is -5ºC, boiling point is 95ºC

questions.question: If you mix a very large bucket of cold water at 10ºC with a small cup of hot water at 90ºC, what will the final temperature of the mixture be closest to?
options: Exactly 50ºC
The temperature of the hot water (90ºC)
The temperature of the cold water (10ºC)
It will freeze instantly to 0ºC

questions.question: What happens to the movement of particles when a cold metal spoon is placed into a bowl of hot water?
options: The water particles move more slowly, and the spoon particles move more quickly
The water particles move more quickly, and the spoon particles move more slowly
Particles in both the water and the spoon stop moving
Only the spoon particles change their speed, while the water particles remain unaffected

questions.question: If you heat one end of a thermal insulator, how does the temperature change along its length?
options: It increases very rapidly to match the heat source
It increases very slowly along the insulator
The temperature decreases instantly below room temperature
It remains completely frozen and never changes

questions.question: Why does thermal insulation prevent the rapid transfer of heat at a particle level?
options: Insulators do not contain any particles that can vibrate
Particles in insulators move from one end to the other instantly
It is difficult for vibrating particles in an insulator to make neighbouring particles vibrate
Insulators absorb all vibrating particles and destroy them

questions.question: Why are materials containing trapped air, like wool or foam, exceptionally good thermal insulators?
options: Air is a dense solid that blocks all particle movement
Gases like air are very poor thermal conductors
Trapped air causes the object's temperature to rise on its own
Air particles are tightly bound and cannot vibrate at all
